content: Miconazole is an antifungal medication prescribed to treat skin infections such as athlete's foot and jock itch, as well as vaginal yeast infections. It may also be used for other conditions as determined by your doctor or pharmacist. Miconazole is available in various forms, including creams, lotions, powders, spray liquids, and spray powders for application to the skin. It also comes in creams and suppositories for vaginal use. For athlete's foot, it is typically applied once or twice daily for one month. For other skin infections, it is used for two weeks. For vaginal infections, it is applied once daily at bedtime for three days (Monistat-3) or seven days (Monistat-7). Follow the instructions on the package or prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use miconazole exactly as directed, and do not use more or less than prescribed. Improvement in skin infections may take several days to become noticeable. When using topical forms of miconazole, apply a small amount to the affected area after thoroughly washing and drying the skin. Gently rub the cream or lotion into the skin and wash your hands immediately afterward. If using vaginal cream or suppositories, follow these steps: 1. Fill the applicator provided with the cream to the indicated level, or unwrap a suppository and place it on the applicator as instructed. 2. Lie on your back with your knees bent and spread apart. 3. Gently insert the applicator into the vagina and push the plunger to release the medication. 4. Remove the applicator. If it is disposable, discard it. If reusable, disassemble and clean it with soap and warm water after each use. 5. Wash your hands promptly to prevent spreading the infection. Apply the dose at bedtime, as it works best when you remain lying down after application. You may wear a sanitary napkin to protect your clothing from stains, but do not use a tampon, as it will absorb the medication. Avoid douching unless instructed by your doctor. Continue using the vaginal cream or suppositories even if you get your period during treatment. Before using miconazole, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to miconazole or any other drugs. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, including vitamins, that you are taking. Notify your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while using miconazole, contact your doctor. If you are using a diaphragm or condom for birth control and are being treated for a vaginal infection, be aware that miconazole vaginal cream and suppositories can interact with latex, so use an alternative method of contraception. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time for your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to make up for a missed one. Miconazole may cause side effects. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience increased burning, itching, or irritation of the skin or vagina, stomach pain, fever, or foul-smelling vaginal discharge. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store miconazole in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. Keep all appointments with your doctor. Miconazole is for external use only. Avoid contact with your eyes, nose, or mouth, and do not swallow it. Do not apply dressings, bandages, cosmetics, lotions, or other skin medications to the treated area unless directed by your doctor. If you purchased miconazole without a prescription and your symptoms do not improve within four weeks (or two weeks for jock itch), stop using it and consult a pharmacist or doctor. If this is your first time experiencing vaginal itching and discomfort, consult a doctor before using miconazole. If you have previously been diagnosed with a yeast infection and have the same symptoms again, use the vaginal cream or suppositories as directed on the package. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription. If your symptoms persist after completing the miconazole treatment, contact your doctor.
